title: Cross-Desk Reference — The Relationship Allowance on a Lateness Charge, Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

# Cross-Desk Reference — The Relationship Allowance on a Lateness Charge, Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

Where the customer charged for a lateness on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan also has a piece at the bench under the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service, the finance desk grants a relationship allowance against the charge. The desk reads the standing of the customer's bench work order and the number of times that piece has been back to the bench.

| The customer's piece at the workshop | The relationship allowance |
|---|---|
| The chain has not yet handed it back, **and** it has been back to the bench at least once | This desk's service-recovery allowance of **20.00 USD** |
| The chain has not yet handed it back, **and** it has not been back to the bench | This desk's open-order allowance of **10.00 USD** |
| Any other case, including a customer with no piece at the workshop | No relationship allowance is granted |

A piece the chain has already handed back falls in the third row however many times it went back to the bench, and a customer holding no work order at all falls there too.

## What is read from the work order

The standing of the work order under the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service says whether the chain still holds the piece, and the record of that order says how many times the piece has been back to the bench. Neither the pricing nor any other rule of that service bears on the allowance; only the standing and the count do.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A customer whose ring is at the workshop and has been back to the bench twice: 20.00 USD.
- A customer whose pendant is at the workshop and has never been back to the bench: 10.00 USD.
- A customer whose bracelet came back from the workshop last month, having been to the bench twice: no relationship allowance.
